name: Unique Normalization Rewriting Diagrams
description: Develops first-order rewriting, decreasing diagrams and conditional linearizations for unique normal forms. Down is a consistency invariant and KO7 lies outside with a printed Lemma 64 counterexample.

program.name: The Confluence Axis
program.summary: The equality test eqW merges two copies of one term that differ only in place: the reflexive diagonal is the one root obstruction to confluence, the disequality guard that repairs it is the greatest conservative repair and is definable by no term of the signature, and the guarded relation terminates and has unique normal forms while the unguarded closure gives eqW void void two normal forms. For first-order rewriting, non-omega-overlap with right-hand-side determinedness gives unique normal forms under the Section 7 hypothesis of Kahrs and Smith, and a three-term counterexample refutes their Lemma 64, the step the published proof of Problem 79 rests on.

oneLine: First-order rewriting with conditional hub linearizations and decreasing diagrams yields unique normal forms under non-omega-overlap and variable conditions, while Down stays a consistency invariant and the printed Lemma 64 promotion with KO7 lies outside.
summary: The theory studies first-order term rewriting, conditional rewriting with level stratification, and the unique-normal-form properties UNconv and UNred. It asks when local conditions such as non-omega-overlap, right-hand-side determinedness and absence of feasible overlaps upgrade to confluence and uniqueness. It develops the Down invariant on finite coalgebras with Horn and executable closures, the constructor translation with consistency invariants, and hub linearizations with decreasing-diagram labels. It proves confluence from decreasing local peaks, from critical-pair joinability with termination or measures, and transfer of confluence of linearizations to unique normal forms. It classifies infinite carriers as those admitting model certificates for R-infinity and its duplicating family. It refutes the printed Lemma 64 implication with a three-node chain where consistency, targeting and completeness hold without universality, and it places Huet and KO7 outside the non-overlap class.
boundary: On one side Down and DownOn are least closed consistency invariants that absorb rewriting and support Horn and finite-table computation, and complete targeted graphs can be universal when root steps are represented. On the other side the three-node d(x) to x carrier satisfies the consistency invariant, targeting and completeness yet fails universality because the bar of Down relates once and twice while the bar of graph equality does not. The obstruction is the missing root representation together with non-joinable KO7 and Huet peaks, and the counterexample to Lemma 64 as printed marks the dividing line for promotion from Down arguments to graph equality.

conclusions.statement: For every labelled step, if all local peaks are decreasing for LevelLabelLt then the unlabelled relation is confluent.
Assuming decidable equality on symbols and variables, for every TRS R, the renamed system is locally confluent if and only if every critical pair of R is joinable in the renamed system.
For any TRS R and conditional system C, if C is a linearization of R and C is confluent then R has unique normal forms for conversion.

Given a well-founded relation, decidable equality on symbols and variables, a TRS R and a measure on renamed terms strictly decreasing on every renamed step, if every critical pair of R is joinable then the renamed step relation is absolutely confluent.
If a relation satisfies the diamond property then its reflexive-transitive closure is confluent.
For any relation r, the Church-Rosser property holds if and only if confluence holds.
If the reverse of a relation is well-founded and the relation is abstractly locally confluent then it is abstractly confluent.
For any carrier list A, system R and terms a and b, DownOn holds for a and b if and only if the Horn derivation from downFacts and downRule derives the pair.
If C is a linearization of R then for all terms s and t, conditional conversion in C holds if and only if conversion in R holds.
If R satisfies ConstructorRules and is strongly almost non-omega-overlapping then Down R is a consistency invariant.
For every type M, HasCertificate for capacity_rules holds if and only if M is infinite.
For every duplication count r and every type M, HasCertificate for family_rules r holds if and only if M is infinite.
ConsistencyInvariantOn holds for DownOn on the fixed carrier and rule, and it is not the case that every targeted proof graph with complete graph is universal.
The pair once and twice is related by bar of DownOn on the fixed carrier and is not related by bar of the graph equality.
The KO7 system is right-hand-side determined, is neither non-overlapping nor non-omega-overlapping, fails unique normal forms for conversion and reduction, and its diagonal peak is not joinable.

openPoints: Finite-carrier transitivity of DownOn for constructor translations of non-omega-overlapping right-determined systems is carried as an unproved hypothesis.
Existence of a complete targeted proof graph representing all root steps on every finite coalgebra is carried as an unproved finite-model supply.
Building a model certificate for every non-omega-overlapping system remains open and would settle RTA problem 79.
The minimal-level labelling uses a peak-dependent unifier rank that is not an intrinsic step label.
